structured_output.hypothesis: In measured sunflower capitula, the crossing angle between the two families of contiguous parastichies stays roughly constant across the disc (isogonal), and angles within a few degrees of 90 degrees are found in only a small minority of heads and radii.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using floret-centre coordinates from at least 30 capitula, compute the local crossing angle between the two contiguous parastichy families in radial annuli. Both conditions must hold. (1) Isogonality: within each head, the coefficient of variation of the crossing angle across annuli from 20% to 100% of disc radius is below 0.10 for at least 80% of heads. (2) Orthogonality is infrequent: the fraction of head-annulus measurements with |angle - 90 deg| <= 5 deg is below 0.20.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if either condition fails. That means the crossing angle varies systematically with radius (CV of 0.10 or more in more than 20% of heads), or the fraction of measurements within 5 degrees of 90 degrees is 0.20 or more, so that orthogonality is the typical case.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'spirals' are the visible parastichies, which are the contiguous Fibonacci families such as 21/34 or 34/55. 'Isogonal' means the angle between the two families is constant along the spirals and across the disc. That is the property of logarithmic spirals about a common pole. 'Orthogonal' means a crossing angle of 90 degrees, which Church's model assumed. 'Infrequent' is operationalised as under 20% of measurements within 5 degrees of 90 degrees. Modern reinterpretation: real florets sit on a generative (Vogel-type) lattice, and parastichies are only approximately logarithmic spirals. The crossing angle is therefore estimated from local lattice vectors between neighbouring florets, not from fitted spiral curves.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I could not identify a public dataset with a title, URL or DOI I am sure exists that gives per-floret centre coordinates or parastichy crossing angles for sunflower capitula. The general portals I know (GBIF, MorphoSource, Dryad, Zenodo) hold specimen occurrence records, 3D scans and unrelated trait data. None is known to hold the floret-position data this test needs. Naming a specific supplement from memory would risk a fabricated identifier, so I am leaving the dataset null. The test would be run on floret-coordinate data from digitised sunflower head images, once such a deposit is located and verified.
